headline: Warming is speeding up, and seven of Earth's sixteen vital signs hit records
why: A sevenfold faster warming rate than last century commits oceans and ice to changes that will keep unfolding long after anyone alive today.

headline: For the first time, people over 65 outnumber children under five worldwide
why: Humanity has always been young. An ageing species changes work, care, pensions, politics and growth in ways historians will treat as an era shift.

headline: Seven in ten people now live where families have fewer than two children
why: Below-replacement fertility across most of the world points to the first sustained global population decline outside of plague and war.

headline: An AI system disproves an 80-year-old Erdős geometry conjecture
why: Checked by outside mathematicians, it marks machines producing original mathematics, a capability that could change how all of science discovers things.

headline: Renewables passed coal as the world's biggest power source in 2025
why: Coal has led electricity for over a century. Clean sources now cover all new demand, the likely turning point of the fossil age.

headline: Artemis II brings the first crew back from the Moon in over 50 years
why: After half a century, humans travelled farther from Earth than ever, reopening crewed deep space with the aim of staying rather than visiting.

headline: The High Seas Treaty takes effect, covering half the planet's surface
why: For the first time, the ocean beyond national borders gets shared rules and marine protected areas, a framework meant to outlast generations.
